description_full: Fresnillo plc mines, develops, and produces non-ferrous minerals in Mexico. It operates through seven segments: Fresnillo, Saucito, Ciénega, Herradura, Noche Buena, San Julián, and Juanicipio. The company primarily explores for silver, gold, lead, and zinc concentrates. Its projects include the Fresnillo silver mine located in the state of Zacatecas; Saucito mine situated in the state of Zacatecas; Ciénega mine located in the state of Durango; Herradura mine located in the state of Sonora; Noche Buena mine located in the state of Sonora; San Julián mine situated on the border of Chihuahua/Durango states; and Juanicipio mine located in the state of Zacatecas. The company also leases mining equipment; produces lead, silver and zinc concentrates and silver precipitates; produces gold/silver doré bars; mines projects; and provides exploration and administrative services. Fresnillo plc was founded in 1887 and is headquartered in Mexico City, Mexico. Fresnillo plc is a subsidiary of Industrias Peñoles, S.A.B. de C.V.

financial_summary: Fresnillo Plc is a large-cap basic materials business with a $24.5B market cap on $4.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +23% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +12.7pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 29%.

The business throws off $1.9B in free cash flow — roughly 41 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.65× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -12.4% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 36× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 75% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 50% operating margin runs 41pp above the Basic Materials median (10%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.04 across 219 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 26% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 10% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 46% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 62% and a beta of 0.89, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 2.04 vs 5y 0.79), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $150K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 32% in the 2020 crash, 34% in the 2022 bear market and 87% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 57% below its DCF fair value of $77.96, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 5%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $44.77 to $137 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Basic Materials peers: P/E 10.7 vs 16.5, EV/EBITDA 5.8 vs 8.5 and P/FCF 13.0 vs 22.8 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 7.7% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 9.8% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 4.1% annual cash-flow growth, 21pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 10% earns above the cost of capital of 9.1%, but the 1pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.23).
It runs a 29% gross margin and converts 41% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.65x, but high accruals (-12.4% of assets).
ROE of 30% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.6x equity multiplier).
SG&A jumped 19% last year, worth watching.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.9B.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 9.5, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 23.3% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 55% of profits supports about 5.4% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders own 75.0%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 15%.
It returns 2.7% a year to shareholders (4.6% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years.
people: With about 7,348 employees, each generates about $621K of revenue, in line with the Basic Materials median.
That works out to $257K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.1M (3x revenue per employee).
